newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's LUKoil starts proceedings for ADR issue.
newsitem.headline: Russia's LUKoil starts proceedings for ADR issue.

text.p: Russia's LUKoil LKOH.RTS has started proceedings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to issue level one American Depository Receipts on preferred stock, vice-president Leonid Fedun told Reuters.
Fedun, citing SEC regulations, said he could give no timeframe for the planned issue.
"We cannot give that sort of information without permission from the SEC," he said. LUKoil has already issued ADRs on its ordinary shares.
Preferred stock accounts for some 9.1 percent of the capital of LUKoil, Russia's biggest producer of crude oil.
Fedun also said LUKoil was preparing to issue a third tranche of convertible shares, but he gave no details.
Large parts of previous issues of convertible shares have been bought by Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO), LUKoil's largest foreign shareholder with about 7.99 percent of the company.
The Russian government holds 33.09 percent, including shares from a shares-for-loans tender, which gave investors the right to manage a company's shares in exchange for a loan for the government.
LUKoil's first ADRS are already traded on NASD and on the Berlin bourse. One ADR represents four underlying LUKoil shares.
ADRs, issued by many Russian companies, give foreign investors access to existing shares while avoiding Russian settlement systems. They do not raise new capital.
